about.title: Saratoga Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Saratoga's mix of hillside terrain, wooded parks, and busy retail centers along Saratoga Avenue and Saratoga Sunnyvale Road creates plenty of opportunities for uneven pavement, wet flooring, and poorly lit stairways to cause serious falls. Whether the incident happened at a wine-country tasting room, a shopping plaza, or a neighbor's property, California law requires the property owner to have known or reasonably should have known about the hazard before liability attaches. That's why documenting the scene, the surface, and the lighting right away matters so much. We handle premises liability cases in Saratoga and Santa Clara County. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless you recover. If you were hurt in a fall, having an attorney evaluate notice, fault, and evidence early on can make a real difference.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Saratoga Premises Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. We can help identify inspection records, past complaints, or maintenance logs that establish this.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage Fast
items.desc: Many Saratoga retail and business properties record over security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of video can be critical to proving how the hazard formed and how long it existed.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present the facts in a way that fairly accounts for shared responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Saratoga?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city park or public building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to contact us soon after the fall so nothing gets missed.

items.question: What if I fell on a hiking trail or hillside property in Saratoga?
items.answer: Saratoga's hillside parks and trails present unique terrain-related hazards, and liability can depend on whether the trail was public or private and whether a dangerous condition existed that the owner should have addressed. We can help sort out who is responsible and whether any recreational use immunities might apply. Documentation of the exact location and conditions is especially important in these cases.

items.question: Do I need proof the store or property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, under California law you generally need to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and didn't fix or warn about it in time. Evidence like photos of the hazard, witness statements, or maintenance records can help establish this. We can guide you on what evidence strengthens your claim.
